h1: The 7 Best Printers With Automatic Document Feeders of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers With ADF 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven printers with automatic document feeders for home offices, from budget Canon units to laser and EcoTank models.
summary: The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the pick for offices with real paper volume, while the Epson EcoTank ET-4950 wins on long-term ink cost. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the best duplex-focused inkjet, and the Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the cheapest way to get a feeder at all.
intro: Most people shop for a printer by print speed and ink price, then discover months later that the thing they do every week is scan a stack of pages, and they are lifting the lid and feeding sheets one at a time. An automatic document feeder fixes that, but only if the rest of the machine suits how you work.

We reviewed seven all-in-ones that list an automatic document feeder on the spec sheet and ranked them on feeder usefulness, duplex support, running cost, connectivity and fit for a home office. We did not rank any model whose feeder we could not confirm from the listing.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Duplex Laser Printer with ADF
products.verdict: The only laser here, and the one built for a steady daily paper load.
products.description:
The MF753Cdw II is a color laser all-in-one with an automatic document feeder, copier, scanner and fax built in. It prints duplex color at 35 pages per minute and connects over wireless, which is a very different speed class from the inkjets below.

It ranks above the Epson EcoTank ET-4950 because laser output is dry and fast and does not clog when the printer sits idle. The tradeoff is cost: it sits in the $200-500 bucket and toner replacement costs more per color set than refilling an ink tank.

Buy it if your office scans and prints real volume every week and values reliability over photo quality. Skip it if you print a few pages a month, since a cheaper inkjet will do the job.
cons: Toner costs more than tank ink
products.idealFor: Home offices with weekly stacks of documents to print and scan.
products.skipIf: You print only a handful of pages a month.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Wireless Supertank Printer with ADF
products.verdict: Refillable tanks turn a feeder printer into a low-running-cost workhorse.
products.description:
The ET-4950 pairs an automatic document feeder with refillable ink tanks that Epson says deliver up to three years of ink. It adds a 2.4-inch color touchscreen, wireless connectivity and a print speed of 18 pages per minute.

It ranks second because it is slower than the Canon laser, but it makes up for it with far cheaper pages over time. Against the ET-4800 below, the ET-4950 gives you the touchscreen and a newer design at a higher entry cost.

Choose it if you scan and print steadily and want to stop buying cartridges. Be aware that a tank printer costs more to buy than a cartridge model, so the savings only show up with consistent use.
pros: Up to three years of ink
products.idealFor: Steady home-office users who hate buying cartridges.
products.skipIf: You print rarely and the ink would dry out unused.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One with ADF
products.verdict: A feeder and duplex printing at a mid-range price, with an ink subscription option.
products.description:
The 8125e is a wireless all-in-one with an automatic document feeder and duplex printing, aimed squarely at home offices. It includes a three-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable printing features.

It ranks third because it lacks the Epson's refillable tanks and the Canon's laser speed, but it is a tidy middle option for people who mostly print documents and scan stacks. Compared with the older HP 8125 below, it is the newer model in the same family.

Buy it if you want duplex and a feeder without a big spend. The caveat is the Instant Ink trial: a subscription can make sense for light printing, but read the terms before you commit.
products.idealFor: Home offices that duplex print and scan regularly.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest long-term ink cost.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless Supertank Printer with ADF
products.verdict: Cartridge-free printing and a feeder at a lower entry price than the ET-4950.
products.description:
The ET-4800 uses a cartridge-free supertank ink system and includes an automatic document feeder, scanner, copier and fax. It supports both Ethernet and wireless, and it is compact for a supertank model.

It ranks below the ET-4950 because it drops the touchscreen and the newer feature set, but the tank economics are the same idea at a lower price. That makes it the smarter buy for anyone who does not need the extras.

Pick it if you want supertank savings and a wired Ethernet option for a shared desk. Skip it if you want a screen-driven interface for walk-up copying.
products.idealFor: Budget-minded offices that want tank ink and a feeder.
products.skipIf: You want a touchscreen and the latest model.

products.award: Best for Photos and Smart Home
products.name: Canon PIXMA TR8620a All-in-One Printer with ADF
products.verdict: A feeder printer that also handles photos and works with Alexa.
products.description:
The TR8620a adds an automatic document feeder to a printer that also prints photos and documents. It prints, copies, scans and faxes, works with AirPrint and Android, and supports Alexa.

It ranks fifth because the feeder is the main reason to buy this tier of printer, and the Epson and HP models offer stronger long-term running costs. It beats the TR4720 below on photo capability and smart features.

Choose it if photos matter as much as paperwork. Skip it if you want the cheapest page cost, since cartridges cost more than tank refills.
products.idealFor: Households mixing photo printing with document scanning.
products.skipIf: You only print text and want lowest page cost.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One with ADF
products.verdict: Feeder and duplex at a mid-range price, with the same core features as the 8125e.
products.description:
The 8125 lists an automatic document feeder, duplex printing, a three-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable printing features. It is wireless and designed for home offices.

It ranks sixth because the 8125e above carries the same listed feature set, so the choice mostly comes down to which listing is cheaper on the day you shop. It sits in the $100-200 bucket, a step cheaper than the 8125e.

Buy it if you want an HP feeder printer and the price is right. The caveat is that the two models read near-identical on paper, so check the exact model number before you order.
products.idealFor: Budget-aware home offices wanting an HP feeder printer.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest ink cost per page.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer with ADF
products.verdict: The cheapest route to a feeder, sized for occasional multi-page scanning.
products.description:
The TR4720 is a compact wireless all-in-one that prints, scans, copies and faxes, with an automatic document feeder for standard paper. It supports mobile printing and costs under $100.

This one lands at the bottom since it targets light use with no duplex or tank advantage, yet it is the cheapest way here to stop feeding pages by hand. Every pick above it costs more and does more.

Buy it for occasional multi-page text scans on a small desk. Skip it if you will print or scan daily.
products.idealFor: Occasional scanners on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You scan or print every day.

methodology.title: Feeder confirmation
methodology.description: We only ranked models whose listing names an automatic document feeder, and dropped any we could not confirm.

methodology.title: Running cost
methodology.description: We compared tank, toner and cartridge systems, since ink spend usually outweighs the purchase price within a couple of years.

methodology.title: Duplex support
methodology.description: Automatic two-sided printing earned credit because it halves paper use for document-heavy offices.

methodology.title: Speed and class
methodology.description: We weighed rated print speed and whether the machine is laser or inkjet, per the spec sheet.

methodology.title: Connectivity
methodology.description: We checked wireless, Ethernet and mobile printing support for shared and small-desk setups.

whatMatters.detail: An automatic document feeder pulls a stack of pages through the scanner without you lifting the lid for each one. It matters because scanning a ten-page contract by hand is slow and error-prone. Check the listing bullets for the words automatic document feeder, not just scanner.
Duplex means the printer prints on both sides of the page automatically. It saves paper and makes reports look professional. Confirm it is automatic duplex, since some listings mean manual flipping.

Cartridge, tank and toner systems differ sharply in cost per page. Tank printers like the Epson EcoTank models cost more upfront but save on refills for steady users. Check whether the listing says refillable tank or cartridge before you buy.

Rated pages per minute tells you how long a stack takes. A 35 PPM laser clears a long report far faster than an 18 PPM inkjet. Look for the PPM figure in the specs, and remember it measures black text, not photos.

Wireless is standard, but Ethernet helps a shared desk stay reliable. Mobile standards like AirPrint let phones print without drivers. Look for the exact protocols in the listing, not just the word wireless.

howToChoose.intro: Volume decides which machine pays back its price.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Laser uses toner fused by heat, so it prints fast and does not clog when idle. The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the laser pick here.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Inkjet is cheaper upfront and better for photos, but ink can dry out if unused. The Epson EcoTank ET-4950, HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e and Canon PIXMA TR8620a are inkjets.

howToChoose.note: Most home offices should default to inkjet unless they print daily, in which case the Canon laser is worth the jump.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact body, a feeder, wireless, and ideally Ethernet if more than one person prints.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 is compact for a supertank and offers Ethernet, while the Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the smallest budget option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print or scan daily. The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II and Epson EcoTank ET-4950 pay back their price in speed and ink savings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You scan occasionally. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 gives you the feeder at the lowest cost here.

faq.q: Do all-in-one printers with a feeder also scan double-sided pages?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The listings here confirm a feeder and, for the HP models, duplex printing, but they do not state duplex scanning. Check the specific model's scanner specs before relying on it.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying a feeder printer?
faq.a: Assuming every all-in-one has a feeder. Many only have a flatbed glass. Always find the words automatic document feeder in the listing.

faq.q: Is an EcoTank worth it over a cartridge printer?
faq.a: If you print steadily, yes, because refillable tanks cut ink spend. If you print rarely, the higher upfront cost may never pay back.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless feeder printer?
faq.a: Connect it to your Wi-Fi from the printer screen or companion app, then add it on your computer or phone. AirPrint and Android printing work without extra drivers on supported models.

faq.q: Do I need to maintain the feeder?
faq.a: Wipe the feeder rollers and scanner glass occasionally to avoid streaks and jams. Use standard paper and avoid stapled or curled pages.

faq.q: Can I use a feeder printer for fax?
faq.a: Several picks list fax, including the Canon and Epson models. You will still need a phone line and should check the model's fax details first.

finalTake: For most offices with serious paper volume, the Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the best feeder printer here. If low ink cost matters most, choose the Epson EcoTank ET-4950. If you only need to stop feeding pages by hand now and then, the Canon PIXMA TR4720 does the job for the least money.
